harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: node1 now serves HTTPS on TCP/8443 using nginx. A persistent systemd timer checks twice daily and renews certificates seven days before expiration. Atomic certificate replacement and nginx reloads preserve availability. Configuration, certificate, firewall rule, and timer survived the required reboot.
actions_performed: Installed nginx and OpenSSL from RHEL repositories.
Generated the TLS private key and certificate locally on node1.
Configured nginx HTTPS on IPv4 and IPv6 port 8443.
Configured atomic certificate rotation with a 30-day lifetime and seven-day renewal threshold.
Enabled a persistent twice-daily systemd renewal timer.
Demonstrated forced and expiry-triggered certificate rotations without failed requests.
Safely rebooted node1 and verified complete recovery.

evidence.summary: Shows active/enabled nginx, IPv4/IPv6 listeners on 8443, successful HTTPS responses, and matching disk/served certificates before and after reboot.

evidence.requirement: Renew the certificate automatically before expiration
evidence.summary: The normal systemd renewal service detected a one-day certificate within the seven-day renewal window and replaced it with a 30-day certificate; the served serial changed accordingly.

evidence.requirement: Pick up each new certificate while continuing to answer requests
evidence.summary: Two rotations changed the served certificate serial. Availability probes recorded 120/120 and 80/80 successful HTTP 200 responses during the respective rotations.
Captures the healthy pre-restart state and boot ID, reboot acknowledgement, changed boot ID, and recovered nginx listener, HTTPS response, certificate, renewal timer, and firewall rule.
